RagShortTexts: The standing military of Hibernians in 374 AD relied upon veteran formations specialized in disciplined field deployment.
Combining heavy protective armor with specialized assault weaponry, the troops executed tactical doctrines honed in frontier engagements.
Commanders emphasized coordinated shock charges and defensive stability, preventing frontline collapse against aggressive cavalry raids.

Variants.Content: The martial renown of Hibernians rested upon exhaustive drilling and veteran battlefield cohesion during the turbulent close of the 4th century. Core tactical doctrine integrated heavy shield formations with disciplined skirmishing wings, executing tactical maneuvers designed to absorb and counter enemy shock. Along vulnerable sectors, defensive engineers implemented field fortifications and obstacles, breaking the initial momentum of hostile assaults. Once enemy ranks faltered, armored shock reserves counter-charged under thunderous horn blasts, crushing exposed flanks with heavy swords and barbed spears. This balance of resilient endurance and ferocious striking power formed the military bedrock preserving Hibernians against overwhelming regional adversaries.

The line stands in a narrow glen, javelins ready and round shields raised. The front rank throws its spears at the charging raiders, then draws swords as the enemy closes. Men on the flank are told to hold their ground at all costs, and a warrior who runs drags his whole kin group into disgrace.

On a ridge above the glen, the positions are studied and messengers go to the flanking warbands. Victory depends on holding the narrow pass until mounted riders can strike the raiders' rear. Each tuath's contingent is judged by its discipline, and the chieftains will remember which kin groups broke first.
